headline: Agilent grows revenue 9.6% with a 30% operating margin and guides fiscal 2027 EPS up about 7% to $6.73–6.86
takeaway: Revenue rose 9.6% to $2.04 billion, or 8.3% core, and adjusted EPS climbed 17% to $1.86, helped by tariff refunds. All three divisions grew, led by applied markets at 13%. Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for 5–7% core growth and EPS of $6.73–6.86. The shares rose 4.2% the next day.
results: Revenue was $2.04 billion, up 9.6% reported and 8.3% on a core basis. Life Sciences and Diagnostics grew 12% to $843 million (9% core) at a 25.9% margin; CrossLab, the services and consumables arm, grew 6% to $799 million at a 34.5% margin; and Applied Markets grew 13% to $398 million at a 29.4% margin.

The adjusted operating margin reached 30.0%, including about 1.2 points from tariff refunds, up 2.8 points from a year earlier. GAAP EPS was $1.59 and adjusted EPS $1.86, up 17%. For the full year, revenue grew 8.7% to $7.55 billion and adjusted EPS 13% to $6.34.
mgmt: Chief executive Padraig McDonnell credited the Ignite operating system, Agilent’s internal efficiency programme, for lifting both growth and margins, and said the company enters 2027 from a position of strength with confidence in outpacing its end markets, including opportunities from AI and autonomous laboratories.

For fiscal 2027 Agilent expects revenue of $8.00 to $8.15 billion, 5% to 7% core growth, and adjusted EPS of $6.73 to $6.86. Excluding the tariff-refund benefit in 2026, that is 8.5% to 10.5% EPS growth. First-quarter revenue is guided to $1.96 to $2.00 billion with EPS of $1.54 to $1.57.
view: This was the quarter that confirmed the laboratory-equipment recovery. After two years of weak instrument orders from pharma and China, Agilent grew every division, and applied markets such as food, environmental and chemical testing grew at double digits. Margins expanding nearly three points, partly from refunds but mostly from cost work, show the efficiency programme is real.

The guidance is deliberately conservative. Core growth of 5% to 7% is below the 8% just delivered, and the EPS range excludes any further tariff refunds. That leaves room for raises through the year if instrument replacement continues, which is presumably why the shares rose 4.2% to $183.52 before giving back some of the gain the following day.

At about 26 times next year’s EPS, Agilent is not cheap, but it trades in line with high-quality peers such as Thermo Fisher and Waters. Most revenue now comes from recurring services and consumables, which supports the multiple. The risks are a renewed slowdown in pharma spending, policy changes for US research funding, and competition in mass spectrometry; the reward is a steady high-single-digit earner with expanding margins.
watch: Instrument order trends in pharma and China, whether core growth runs above the 5–7% guide in the first half, and margin progress without the help of tariff refunds.
